g.text: SITE B — Chicago · arm64 · 2 OCPU / 12 GB · STANDBY

text.tspan: k3s's Kubernetes datastore must NOT be stretched across sites — it writes
constantly (node leases, events, status), so a ~50 ms hop lands on every
commit. The witness DCS is the same technology with a workload three orders
of magnitude smaller: a handful of tiny writes per minute. Stretching THAT
is correct. Same tool, opposite answer, and the write rate is why.
Three nodes cannot satisfy both — so the data
replicates asynchronously and needs no quorum,
and only the ARBITRATION is quorate.
only one holder can exist at a time
no data · no traffic · no replica
if the agent hangs, the host reboots
BEFORE it can write as a stale primary
the node it monitors cannot report
an untested backup is a belief
Site A dies → B + witness are a majority.
B wins the lock, promotes. AUTOMATIC.

g.text: Site B dies → leader keeps its lock. Nothing happens.

text.tspan: WITNESS dies → both databases keep running.
A <-> B link cut → both still reach the witness.
A keeps the lock, B cannot take it.

g.text: may acquire ONLY if it wins CAS
